ov: About 220 species of flat, cartilaginous fish with a venomous barbed stinger on the tail, common in warm coastal seas worldwide; some live in rivers or the deep ocean. Most lie on the sea floor, camouflaged against the sand, and their mouths are on the underside of the body.

why.dg: A sting is very painful but rarely fatal. Steve Irwin’s death in 2006 was only the second recorded in Australian waters since 1945.
why.et: Rays are edible, and stingray dishes are found on coasts worldwide.

rg: Tropical and subtropical coastal waters worldwide; river stingrays in fresh water.
df: Mostly molluscs and crustaceans, occasionally small fish. They find prey with electrical sensors around the mouth, and Amazon river stingrays eat insects.
fx: Stingrays give birth to live young, in litters of five to thirteen.
notes: Group entry. The existing fact is broadly confirmed: the blade is "deeply barbed and usually breaks off in the wound"; "purely defensive" isn’t stated.
